ACH50 Building Tightness 0-1.5 Very Tight 1.5-3 Tight 3-5 Moderately Tight 5-7 Loose 7-10 Very Loose 10+ Extremely Loose The three units of Moore Street Senior Apartments tested loose to very loose in terms of relative air tightness, indicating potential opportunities for air sealing improvements that could help reduce energy usage and costs, increase occupant comfort, and reduce air exchange between neighboring units. 3.7 Health and Safety The building has fire and smoke alarms with battery backup as well as fire extinguishers throughout the building. During the on-site survey, staff did not observe any mold on interior building surfaces. The building manager reported one issue that has arisen in the last decade of poor indoor air quality in the hotter summers in Fairbanks, especially when there are wildfires burning in the forests that neighbor the Fairbanks area. With no dedicated balanced ventilation system, the building relies on exhaust-only ventilation consisting of bath fans controlled by humidistats and range hoods with on/off controls in individual units. When these place the building into a negative pressure, air comes in through cracks in the building envelope. There is no filtration, and in the summer, residents bring in smokey air when they use exhaust ventilation. On particularly smokey days, the building manager has reported that you could see visible smoke when you look down the long hallway.
